children: Brazil extended measures aimed at curbing fuel price increases to keep providing consumers with a price buffer before the first round of the presidential election on October 4. According to Sina Finance, the Finance Ministry said the diesel subsidy of 2.12 reais per liter, which was due to expire on Saturday, will be extended for at least 30 more days under a temporary measure that took effect on May 30, and the extension does not change the subsidy amount. This month, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva announced further fuel tax cuts to protect consumers from the impact of surging oil prices caused by the U.S.-Iran war. The measures also include tax cuts on gasoline and ethanol.

title: Brazil Extends Fuel Price Subsidies Ahead of Election
